discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moire and rhombohedral graphene materials

nominees.name: Kin Fai Mak
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids, Dresden, Germany / Cornell University, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum matter
motivation: For four decades, fractionally charged anyons were seen only in the fractional quantum Hall effect, which needs strong magnetic fields. Theory predicted that interacting electrons in topological flat bands could form fractional Chern insulators with no applied field at all. In 2023-2024 the nominees made this prediction real. Xu's group in twisted MoTe2 found it through optical and transport signatures, Mak's group (with Jie Shan) found quantized fractional Hall resistance in the same material, and Ju's group found it in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN. These experiments show that lattice band topology combined with interactions alone can produce fractionalized phases. That opens a new field: fractional and possibly non-Abelian anyons in tunable, gate-controlled materials at zero field, with clear prospects for topological quantum computation. This is a clear case of abstract topological theory being realized in the laboratory, and it is already reshaping quantum matter research worldwide.
